implementer.deviations:
1. The spec's local `Line` type did not get `updatedAt`, because OrderLineSchema has no updatedAt and the reply would never carry it. Test 6 reads `updated_at::text` from the database instead (microsecond precision). `discountBps` was added to the type for the charged-line assertion.
2. Added a ninth test (orders.spec) for amendment (e), which the verdict's "what the verifier must prove" requires. The plan lists eight.
3. The failing tests were not committed separately. STEP 4 prescribes one commit, so the failing output is kept in the scratchpad (dos126-orders-before.txt, dos126-trap.txt) and in failBefore.
4. The lane's command form `pnpm --filter @dos/core test -- <file>` runs the whole core suite under pnpm 11, because the literal `--` makes vitest drop the file and -t filters. It happened once, on the first pre-fix run (36 files, only the 9 new tests failed). Every later run used `pnpm --filter @dos/core exec vitest run <file>`. The last four single-file runs (warehouse, delivery, ai, orders) were separate commands sent concurrently.
5. Backend `pnpm format` also reformatted pricing.spec.ts, which I never touched. Its DOS-096 test was committed unformatted in 7f7fc8b. I restored the file with `git restore` (my own worktree only) and did not commit it.
6. repriceApprovedBargains:
   - The pre-check looks only at lines with qtyPcs > 0, as the engine does.
   - The quote still receives every stored line, so order-level scheme allocation matches the draft.
   - A changed line is `{ ...storedLine, ...pricedLineFields(q) }`, so id, lineNo, entered qty/unit, packSizeAtEntry, qtyPcs, picked/delivered and createdAt stay unchanged.
7. The CONFLICT from the billing guard carries no `data` field; the amendment only asks that it name the order line.
8. The commit message has two Test: lines (orders and billing), because both halves land in this commit.
